August 11, 2026 12:02 ET | Source: Research and Markets Research and Markets Dublin, Aug.  11, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The "Hyperscale Data Center Market, Till 2040: Distribution by Type of Component, Type of Deployment, Data Center Size, End User, Type of Workload, Cooling Technology, Geographical Regions, and Leading Players: Industry Trends and Global Forecasts" has been added to ResearchAndMarkets.com's offering. Global Hyperscale Data Center Market Projected to Reach USD 1.21 Trillion by 2040 as AI Infrastructure Investment Accelerates The global hyperscale data center market is projected to increase from USD 245.0 billion in 2026 to USD 1.21 trillion by 2040, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 12.1%. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure. Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Major cloud service providers and infrastructure operators are also integrating renewable energy procurement into development strategies as sustainability regulations and grid constraints influence site selection. Recent transactions demonstrate the strategic importance of hyperscale infrastructure. Alphabet's acquisition of renewable energy developer Intersect in December 2025 reflected the growing convergence of clean energy and data center development. Industry confidence was further illustrated by the USD 40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers by a consortium comprising BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI. Key Hyperscale Data Center Market Findings IT infrastructure is projected to represent 34.0% of the global market in 2026, while liquid cooling systems are expected to record the fastest growth through 2040. Cloud deployment is anticipated to account for 46.0% of the market in 2026. Multi-cloud deployment is forecast to expand at a CAGR of 14.7% through 2040. Massive hyperscale facilities are estimated to capture 49.0% of the market in 2026 as operators prioritize centralized, high-capacity infrastructure. Cloud computing workloads are expected to hold a 31.0% market share in 2026, supported by enterprise migration and digital service growth. North America is projected to lead with a 41.0% share in 2026. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region, registering a CAGR of 14.5% through 2040. Competitive Landscape and Investment Outlook The hyperscale data center industry is increasingly characterized by vertically integrated cloud and AI infrastructure ecosystems. Leading operators maintain extensive control over computing resources, networking, AI accelerators, software platforms and energy procurement. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Amazon has projected approximately USD 200 billion in 2026 capital spending, compared with approximately USD 125 billion in the previous year. Microsoft allocated USD 80 billion during 2025 to AI-optimized data centers and Azure infrastructure. Alphabet committed approximately USD 75 billion in 2025 and is expected to raise capital expenditure to between USD 175 billion and USD 185 billion in 2026. Startup and growth-stage investment is also accelerating. Approximately 70% of data center-focused companies that raised more than USD 500 million completed their latest equity financing rounds during 2024 or 2025. CoreWeave has expanded its AI cloud infrastructure footprint to 32 data center facilities and approximately 250,000 GPUs as of 2025. Vantage Data Centers secured more than USD 2 billion in Series C financing in January 2026 after receiving an additional USD 1.6 billion equity investment in November 2025. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability. Growth Opportunities in AI, Multi-Cloud and Sovereign Infrastructure Multi-cloud adoption and sovereign AI initiatives are creating opportunities for hyperscale development, specialized AI-ready facilities and strategic infrastructure partnerships. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services. Thermal management will remain a central investment priority as rack densities increase. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling and hybrid cooling systems are expected to gain adoption across AI and high-performance computing environments. Power availability will also shape future development, encouraging collaboration among hyperscale operators, utilities, renewable energy developers, semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure investors. Market Segmentation Covered in the Report The hyperscale data center market report evaluates opportunities by component, deployment model, facility size, end user, workload, cooling technology and geography. Components: IT infrastructure, servers, storage systems, networking equipment, power infrastructure, cooling infrastructure, construction, security and monitoring solutions. Deployment models: Cloud, colocation, on-premises, hybrid and multi-cloud. Facility sizes: Small and medium facilities, large facilities and massive hyperscale facilities. End users: Cloud and colocation providers, enterprises, government agencies, telecommunications companies, digital platforms, financial institutions, healthcare organizations and retailers. Workloads: AI and machine learning, big data analytics, cloud computing, content delivery, enterprise applications, high-performance computing, IoT and edge processing. Cooling technologies: Air cooling, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, hybrid cooling and free cooling systems. Regions: North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, the Middle East and North Africa, and the rest of the world. Strategic Value for Decision-Makers The report supports infrastructure investment, market entry, technology planning and regional expansion decisions across the hyperscale data center ecosystem. It identifies market gaps in liquid cooling, power availability, sovereign AI capacity and high-density networking while examining funding activity involving cloud providers, AI infrastructure companies, cooling technology developers and renewable energy-linked projects. Decision-makers can use the analysis to benchmark competitive positioning, assess acquisition opportunities, evaluate infrastructure financing and identify potential partnerships. The report also reviews direct-to-chip cooling, immersion cooling, AI accelerators, multi-cloud orchestration and advanced thermal management technologies. Additional modules include market sizing and opportunity analysis, company profiles, competitive benchmarking, megatrend assessment, patent analysis, recent industry developments, Porter's Five Forces analysis and SWOT analysis. Forecasts extend through 2040 and cover revenue opportunities across deployment models, components, workloads, cooling technologies, end users and geographic markets. The report addresses the current and future hyperscale data center market size, leading companies, principal growth drivers, partnership and funding trends, regional growth prospects and the distribution of opportunities across major market segments. Purchasers also receive dynamic Excel dashboards, up to 15% complimentary content customization, an interactive report walkthrough and qualifying report updates. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure. Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability. Growth Opportunities in AI, Multi-Cloud and Sovereign Infrastructure Multi-cloud adoption and sovereign AI initiatives are creating opportunities for hyperscale development, specialized AI-ready facilities and strategic infrastructure partnerships. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services. Thermal management will remain a central investment priority as rack densities increase. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling and hybrid cooling systems are expected to gain adoption across AI and high-performance computing environments. Power availability will also shape future development, encouraging collaboration among hyperscale operators, utilities, renewable energy developers, semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure investors. Global Hyperscale Data Center Market Projected to Reach USD 1.21 Trillion by 2040 as AI Infrastructure Investment Accelerates The global hyperscale data center market is projected to increase from USD 245.0 billion in 2026 to USD 1.21 trillion by 2040, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 12.1%. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure. Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Major cloud service providers and infrastructure operators are also integrating renewable energy procurement into development strategies as sustainability regulations and grid constraints influence site selection. Recent transactions demonstrate the strategic importance of hyperscale infrastructure. Alphabet's acquisition of renewable energy developer Intersect in December 2025 reflected the growing convergence of clean energy and data center development. Industry confidence was further illustrated by the USD 40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers by a consortium comprising BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI. Key Hyperscale Data Center Market Findings IT infrastructure is projected to represent 34.0% of the global market in 2026, while liquid cooling systems are expected to record the fastest growth through 2040. Cloud deployment is anticipated to account for 46.0% of the market in 2026. Multi-cloud deployment is forecast to expand at a CAGR of 14.7% through 2040. Massive hyperscale facilities are estimated to capture 49.0% of the market in 2026 as operators prioritize centralized, high-capacity infrastructure. Cloud computing workloads are expected to hold a 31.0% market share in 2026, supported by enterprise migration and digital service growth. North America is projected to lead with a 41.0% share in 2026. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region, registering a CAGR of 14.5% through 2040. Competitive Landscape and Investment Outlook The hyperscale data center industry is increasingly characterized by vertically integrated cloud and AI infrastructure ecosystems. Leading operators maintain extensive control over computing resources, networking, AI accelerators, software platforms and energy procurement. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Amazon has projected approximately USD 200 billion in 2026 capital spending, compared with approximately USD 125 billion in the previous year. Microsoft allocated USD 80 billion during 2025 to AI-optimized data centers and Azure infrastructure. Alphabet committed approximately USD 75 billion in 2025 and is expected to raise capital expenditure to between USD 175 billion and USD 185 billion in 2026. Startup and growth-stage investment is also accelerating. Approximately 70% of data center-focused companies that raised more than USD 500 million completed their latest equity financing rounds during 2024 or 2025. CoreWeave has expanded its AI cloud infrastructure footprint to 32 data center facilities and approximately 250,000 GPUs as of 2025. Vantage Data Centers secured more than USD 2 billion in Series C financing in January 2026 after receiving an additional USD 1.6 billion equity investment in November 2025. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability. Growth Opportunities in AI, Multi-Cloud and Sovereign Infrastructure Multi-cloud adoption and sovereign AI initiatives are creating opportunities for hyperscale development, specialized AI-ready facilities and strategic infrastructure partnerships. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services. Thermal management will remain a central investment priority as rack densities increase. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling and hybrid cooling systems are expected to gain adoption across AI and high-performance computing environments. Power availability will also shape future development, encouraging collaboration among hyperscale operators, utilities, renewable energy developers, semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure investors. Global Hyperscale Data Center Market Projected to Reach USD 1.21 Trillion by 2040 as AI Infrastructure Investment Accelerates The global hyperscale data center market is projected to increase from USD 245.0 billion in 2026 to USD 1.21 trillion by 2040, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 12.1%. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure. Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Major cloud service providers and infrastructure operators are also integrating renewable energy procurement into development strategies as sustainability regulations and grid constraints influence site selection. Recent transactions demonstrate the strategic importance of hyperscale infrastructure. Alphabet's acquisition of renewable energy developer Intersect in December 2025 reflected the growing convergence of clean energy and data center development. Industry confidence was further illustrated by the USD 40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers by a consortium comprising BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI. Key Hyperscale Data Center Market Findings IT infrastructure is projected to represent 34.0% of the global market in 2026, while liquid cooling systems are expected to record the fastest growth through 2040. Cloud deployment is anticipated to account for 46.0% of the market in 2026. Multi-cloud deployment is forecast to expand at a CAGR of 14.7% through 2040. Massive hyperscale facilities are estimated to capture 49.0% of the market in 2026 as operators prioritize centralized, high-capacity infrastructure. Cloud computing workloads are expected to hold a 31.0% market share in 2026, supported by enterprise migration and digital service growth. North America is projected to lead with a 41.0% share in 2026. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region, registering a CAGR of 14.5% through 2040. Competitive Landscape and Investment Outlook The hyperscale data center industry is increasingly characterized by vertically integrated cloud and AI infrastructure ecosystems. Leading operators maintain extensive control over computing resources, networking, AI accelerators, software platforms and energy procurement. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Amazon has projected approximately USD 200 billion in 2026 capital spending, compared with approximately USD 125 billion in the previous year. Microsoft allocated USD 80 billion during 2025 to AI-optimized data centers and Azure infrastructure. Alphabet committed approximately USD 75 billion in 2025 and is expected to raise capital expenditure to between USD 175 billion and USD 185 billion in 2026. Startup and growth-stage investment is also accelerating. Approximately 70% of data center-focused companies that raised more than USD 500 million completed their latest equity financing rounds during 2024 or 2025. CoreWeave has expanded its AI cloud infrastructure footprint to 32 data center facilities and approximately 250,000 GPUs as of 2025. Vantage Data Centers secured more than USD 2 billion in Series C financing in January 2026 after receiving an additional USD 1.6 billion equity investment in November 2025. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability. Growth Opportunities in AI, Multi-Cloud and Sovereign Infrastructure Multi-cloud adoption and sovereign AI initiatives are creating opportunities for hyperscale development, specialized AI-ready facilities and strategic infrastructure partnerships. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services. Thermal management will remain a central investment priority as rack densities increase. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling and hybrid cooling systems are expected to gain adoption across AI and high-performance computing environments. Power availability will also shape future development, encouraging collaboration among hyperscale operators, utilities, renewable energy developers, semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure investors. Global Hyperscale Data Center Market Projected to Reach USD 1.21 Trillion by 2040 as AI Infrastructure Investment Accelerates
The global hyperscale data center market is projected to increase from USD 245.0 billion in 2026 to USD 1.21 trillion by 2040, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 12.1%. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure.
Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Major cloud service providers and infrastructure operators are also integrating renewable energy procurement into development strategies as sustainability regulations and grid constraints influence site selection.
Recent transactions demonstrate the strategic importance of hyperscale infrastructure. Alphabet's acquisition of renewable energy developer Intersect in December 2025 reflected the growing convergence of clean energy and data center development. Industry confidence was further illustrated by the USD 40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers by a consortium comprising BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI.

Competitive Landscape and Investment Outlook
The hyperscale data center industry is increasingly characterized by vertically integrated cloud and AI infrastructure ecosystems. Leading operators maintain extensive control over computing resources, networking, AI accelerators, software platforms and energy procurement. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage.
Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Amazon has projected approximately USD 200 billion in 2026 capital spending, compared with approximately USD 125 billion in the previous year. Microsoft allocated USD 80 billion during 2025 to AI-optimized data centers and Azure infrastructure. Alphabet committed approximately USD 75 billion in 2025 and is expected to raise capital expenditure to between USD 175 billion and USD 185 billion in 2026.
Startup and growth-stage investment is also accelerating. Approximately 70% of data center-focused companies that raised more than USD 500 million completed their latest equity financing rounds during 2024 or 2025. CoreWeave has expanded its AI cloud infrastructure footprint to 32 data center facilities and approximately 250,000 GPUs as of 2025. Vantage Data Centers secured more than USD 2 billion in Series C financing in January 2026 after receiving an additional USD 1.6 billion equity investment in November 2025. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability.
Growth Opportunities in AI, Multi-Cloud and Sovereign Infrastructure
Multi-cloud adoption and sovereign AI initiatives are creating opportunities for hyperscale development, specialized AI-ready facilities and strategic infrastructure partnerships. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services.
Thermal management will remain a central investment priority as rack densities increase. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling and hybrid cooling systems are expected to gain adoption across AI and high-performance computing environments. Power availability will also shape future development, encouraging collaboration among hyperscale operators, utilities, renewable energy developers, semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure investors.

August 11, 2026 12:02 ET | Source: Research and Markets Research and Markets Dublin, Aug.  11, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The "Hyperscale Data Center Market, Till 2040: Distribution by Type of Component, Type of Deployment, Data Center Size, End User, Type of Workload, Cooling Technology, Geographical Regions, and Leading Players: Industry Trends and Global Forecasts" has been added to ResearchAndMarkets.com's offering. Global Hyperscale Data Center Market Projected to Reach USD 1.21 Trillion by 2040 as AI Infrastructure Investment Accelerates The global hyperscale data center market is projected to increase from USD 245.0 billion in 2026 to USD 1.21 trillion by 2040, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 12.1%. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure. Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Major cloud service providers and infrastructure operators are also integrating renewable energy procurement into development strategies as sustainability regulations and grid constraints influence site selection. Recent transactions demonstrate the strategic importance of hyperscale infrastructure. Alphabet's acquisition of renewable energy developer Intersect in December 2025 reflected the growing convergence of clean energy and data center development. Industry confidence was further illustrated by the USD 40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers by a consortium comprising BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI. Key Hyperscale Data Center Market Findings IT infrastructure is projected to represent 34.0% of the global market in 2026, while liquid cooling systems are expected to record the fastest growth through 2040. Cloud deployment is anticipated to account for 46.0% of the market in 2026. Multi-cloud deployment is forecast to expand at a CAGR of 14.7% through 2040. Massive hyperscale facilities are estimated to capture 49.0% of the market in 2026 as operators prioritize centralized, high-capacity infrastructure. Cloud computing workloads are expected to hold a 31.0% market share in 2026, supported by enterprise migration and digital service growth. North America is projected to lead with a 41.0% share in 2026. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region, registering a CAGR of 14.5% through 2040. Competitive Landscape and Investment Outlook The hyperscale data center industry is increasingly characterized by vertically integrated cloud and AI infrastructure ecosystems. Leading operators maintain extensive control over computing resources, networking, AI accelerators, software platforms and energy procurement. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Amazon has projected approximately USD 200 billion in 2026 capital spending, compared with approximately USD 125 billion in the previous year. Microsoft allocated USD 80 billion during 2025 to AI-optimized data centers and Azure infrastructure. Alphabet committed approximately USD 75 billion in 2025 and is expected to raise capital expenditure to between USD 175 billion and USD 185 billion in 2026. Startup and growth-stage investment is also accelerating. Approximately 70% of data center-focused companies that raised more than USD 500 million completed their latest equity financing rounds during 2024 or 2025. CoreWeave has expanded its AI cloud infrastructure footprint to 32 data center facilities and approximately 250,000 GPUs as of 2025. Vantage Data Centers secured more than USD 2 billion in Series C financing in January 2026 after receiving an additional USD 1.6 billion equity investment in November 2025. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability. Growth Opportunities in AI, Multi-Cloud and Sovereign Infrastructure Multi-cloud adoption and sovereign AI initiatives are creating opportunities for hyperscale development, specialized AI-ready facilities and strategic infrastructure partnerships. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services. Thermal management will remain a central investment priority as rack densities increase. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling and hybrid cooling systems are expected to gain adoption across AI and high-performance computing environments. Power availability will also shape future development, encouraging collaboration among hyperscale operators, utilities, renewable energy developers, semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure investors. Market Segmentation Covered in the Report The hyperscale data center market report evaluates opportunities by component, deployment model, facility size, end user, workload, cooling technology and geography. Components: IT infrastructure, servers, storage systems, networking equipment, power infrastructure, cooling infrastructure, construction, security and monitoring solutions. Deployment models: Cloud, colocation, on-premises, hybrid and multi-cloud. Facility sizes: Small and medium facilities, large facilities and massive hyperscale facilities. End users: Cloud and colocation providers, enterprises, government agencies, telecommunications companies, digital platforms, financial institutions, healthcare organizations and retailers. Workloads: AI and machine learning, big data analytics, cloud computing, content delivery, enterprise applications, high-performance computing, IoT and edge processing. Cooling technologies: Air cooling, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, hybrid cooling and free cooling systems. Regions: North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, the Middle East and North Africa, and the rest of the world. Strategic Value for Decision-Makers The report supports infrastructure investment, market entry, technology planning and regional expansion decisions across the hyperscale data center ecosystem. It identifies market gaps in liquid cooling, power availability, sovereign AI capacity and high-density networking while examining funding activity involving cloud providers, AI infrastructure companies, cooling technology developers and renewable energy-linked projects. Decision-makers can use the analysis to benchmark competitive positioning, assess acquisition opportunities, evaluate infrastructure financing and identify potential partnerships. The report also reviews direct-to-chip cooling, immersion cooling, AI accelerators, multi-cloud orchestration and advanced thermal management technologies. Additional modules include market sizing and opportunity analysis, company profiles, competitive benchmarking, megatrend assessment, patent analysis, recent industry developments, Porter's Five Forces analysis and SWOT analysis. Forecasts extend through 2040 and cover revenue opportunities across deployment models, components, workloads, cooling technologies, end users and geographic markets. The report addresses the current and future hyperscale data center market size, leading companies, principal growth drivers, partnership and funding trends, regional growth prospects and the distribution of opportunities across major market segments. Purchasers also receive dynamic Excel dashboards, up to 15% complimentary content customization, an interactive report walkthrough and qualifying report updates. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure. Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Major cloud service providers and infrastructure operators are also integrating renewable energy procurement into development strategies as sustainability regulations and grid constraints influence site selection. Recent transactions demonstrate the strategic importance of hyperscale infrastructure. Alphabet's acquisition of renewable energy developer Intersect in December 2025 reflected the growing convergence of clean energy and data center development. Industry confidence was further illustrated by the USD 40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers by a consortium comprising BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI. Massive hyperscale facilities are estimated to capture 49.0% of the market in 2026 as operators prioritize centralized, high-capacity infrastructure. Cloud computing workloads are expected to hold a 31.0% market share in 2026, supported by enterprise migration and digital service growth. Competitive Landscape and Investment Outlook The hyperscale data center industry is increasingly characterized by vertically integrated cloud and AI infrastructure ecosystems. Leading operators maintain extensive control over computing resources, networking, AI accelerators, software platforms and energy procurement. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Amazon has projected approximately USD 200 billion in 2026 capital spending, compared with approximately USD 125 billion in the previous year. Alphabet committed approximately USD 75 billion in 2025 and is expected to raise capital expenditure to between USD 175 billion and USD 185 billion in 2026. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services. Global Hyperscale Data Center Market Projected to Reach USD 1.21 Trillion by 2040 as AI Infrastructure Investment Accelerates The global hyperscale data center market is projected to increase from USD 245.0 billion in 2026 to USD 1.21 trillion by 2040, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 12.1%. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure. Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Major cloud service providers and infrastructure operators are also integrating renewable energy procurement into development strategies as sustainability regulations and grid constraints influence site selection. Recent transactions demonstrate the strategic importance of hyperscale infrastructure. Alphabet's acquisition of renewable energy developer Intersect in December 2025 reflected the growing convergence of clean energy and data center development. Industry confidence was further illustrated by the USD 40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers by a consortium comprising BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI. Key Hyperscale Data Center Market Findings IT infrastructure is projected to represent 34.0% of the global market in 2026, while liquid cooling systems are expected to record the fastest growth through 2040. Cloud deployment is anticipated to account for 46.0% of the market in 2026. Multi-cloud deployment is forecast to expand at a CAGR of 14.7% through 2040. Massive hyperscale facilities are estimated to capture 49.0% of the market in 2026 as operators prioritize centralized, high-capacity infrastructure. Cloud computing workloads are expected to hold a 31.0% market share in 2026, supported by enterprise migration and digital service growth. North America is projected to lead with a 41.0% share in 2026. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region, registering a CAGR of 14.5% through 2040. Competitive Landscape and Investment Outlook The hyperscale data center industry is increasingly characterized by vertically integrated cloud and AI infrastructure ecosystems. Leading operators maintain extensive control over computing resources, networking, AI accelerators, software platforms and energy procurement. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Amazon has projected approximately USD 200 billion in 2026 capital spending, compared with approximately USD 125 billion in the previous year. Microsoft allocated USD 80 billion during 2025 to AI-optimized data centers and Azure infrastructure. Alphabet committed approximately USD 75 billion in 2025 and is expected to raise capital expenditure to between USD 175 billion and USD 185 billion in 2026. Startup and growth-stage investment is also accelerating. Approximately 70% of data center-focused companies that raised more than USD 500 million completed their latest equity financing rounds during 2024 or 2025. CoreWeave has expanded its AI cloud infrastructure footprint to 32 data center facilities and approximately 250,000 GPUs as of 2025. Vantage Data Centers secured more than USD 2 billion in Series C financing in January 2026 after receiving an additional USD 1.6 billion equity investment in November 2025. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability. Growth Opportunities in AI, Multi-Cloud and Sovereign Infrastructure Multi-cloud adoption and sovereign AI initiatives are creating opportunities for hyperscale development, specialized AI-ready facilities and strategic infrastructure partnerships. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services. Thermal management will remain a central investment priority as rack densities increase. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling and hybrid cooling systems are expected to gain adoption across AI and high-performance computing environments. Power availability will also shape future development, encouraging collaboration among hyperscale operators, utilities, renewable energy developers, semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure investors. Global Hyperscale Data Center Market Projected to Reach USD 1.21 Trillion by 2040 as AI Infrastructure Investment Accelerates The global hyperscale data center market is projected to increase from USD 245.0 billion in 2026 to USD 1.21 trillion by 2040, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 12.1%. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure. Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Major cloud service providers and infrastructure operators are also integrating renewable energy procurement into development strategies as sustainability regulations and grid constraints influence site selection. Recent transactions demonstrate the strategic importance of hyperscale infrastructure. Alphabet's acquisition of renewable energy developer Intersect in December 2025 reflected the growing convergence of clean energy and data center development. Industry confidence was further illustrated by the USD 40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers by a consortium comprising BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI. Key Hyperscale Data Center Market Findings IT infrastructure is projected to represent 34.0% of the global market in 2026, while liquid cooling systems are expected to record the fastest growth through 2040. Cloud deployment is anticipated to account for 46.0% of the market in 2026. Multi-cloud deployment is forecast to expand at a CAGR of 14.7% through 2040. Massive hyperscale facilities are estimated to capture 49.0% of the market in 2026 as operators prioritize centralized, high-capacity infrastructure. Cloud computing workloads are expected to hold a 31.0% market share in 2026, supported by enterprise migration and digital service growth. North America is projected to lead with a 41.0% share in 2026. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region, registering a CAGR of 14.5% through 2040. Competitive Landscape and Investment Outlook The hyperscale data center industry is increasingly characterized by vertically integrated cloud and AI infrastructure ecosystems. Leading operators maintain extensive control over computing resources, networking, AI accelerators, software platforms and energy procurement. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Amazon has projected approximately USD 200 billion in 2026 capital spending, compared with approximately USD 125 billion in the previous year. Microsoft allocated USD 80 billion during 2025 to AI-optimized data centers and Azure infrastructure. Alphabet committed approximately USD 75 billion in 2025 and is expected to raise capital expenditure to between USD 175 billion and USD 185 billion in 2026. Startup and growth-stage investment is also accelerating. Approximately 70% of data center-focused companies that raised more than USD 500 million completed their latest equity financing rounds during 2024 or 2025. CoreWeave has expanded its AI cloud infrastructure footprint to 32 data center facilities and approximately 250,000 GPUs as of 2025. Vantage Data Centers secured more than USD 2 billion in Series C financing in January 2026 after receiving an additional USD 1.6 billion equity investment in November 2025. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability. Growth Opportunities in AI, Multi-Cloud and Sovereign Infrastructure Multi-cloud adoption and sovereign AI initiatives are creating opportunities for hyperscale development, specialized AI-ready facilities and strategic infrastructure partnerships. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services. Thermal management will remain a central investment priority as rack densities increase. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling and hybrid cooling systems are expected to gain adoption across AI and high-performance computing environments. Power availability will also shape future development, encouraging collaboration among hyperscale operators, utilities, renewable energy developers, semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure investors. Global Hyperscale Data Center Market Projected to Reach USD 1.21 Trillion by 2040 as AI Infrastructure Investment Accelerates The global hyperscale data center market is projected to increase from USD 245.0 billion in 2026 to USD 1.21 trillion by 2040, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 12.1%. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure. Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Major cloud service providers and infrastructure operators are also integrating renewable energy procurement into development strategies as sustainability regulations and grid constraints influence site selection. Recent transactions demonstrate the strategic importance of hyperscale infrastructure. Alphabet's acquisition of renewable energy developer Intersect in December 2025 reflected the growing convergence of clean energy and data center development. Industry confidence was further illustrated by the USD 40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers by a consortium comprising BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI. Key Hyperscale Data Center Market Findings IT infrastructure is projected to represent 34.0% of the global market in 2026, while liquid cooling systems are expected to record the fastest growth through 2040. Cloud deployment is anticipated to account for 46.0% of the market in 2026. Multi-cloud deployment is forecast to expand at a CAGR of 14.7% through 2040. Massive hyperscale facilities are estimated to capture 49.0% of the market in 2026 as operators prioritize centralized, high-capacity infrastructure. Cloud computing workloads are expected to hold a 31.0% market share in 2026, supported by enterprise migration and digital service growth. North America is projected to lead with a 41.0% share in 2026. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region, registering a CAGR of 14.5% through 2040. Competitive Landscape and Investment Outlook The hyperscale data center industry is increasingly characterized by vertically integrated cloud and AI infrastructure ecosystems. Leading operators maintain extensive control over computing resources, networking, AI accelerators, software platforms and energy procurement. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Amazon has projected approximately USD 200 billion in 2026 capital spending, compared with approximately USD 125 billion in the previous year. Microsoft allocated USD 80 billion during 2025 to AI-optimized data centers and Azure infrastructure. Alphabet committed approximately USD 75 billion in 2025 and is expected to raise capital expenditure to between USD 175 billion and USD 185 billion in 2026. Startup and growth-stage investment is also accelerating. Approximately 70% of data center-focused companies that raised more than USD 500 million completed their latest equity financing rounds during 2024 or 2025. CoreWeave has expanded its AI cloud infrastructure footprint to 32 data center facilities and approximately 250,000 GPUs as of 2025. Vantage Data Centers secured more than USD 2 billion in Series C financing in January 2026 after receiving an additional USD 1.6 billion equity investment in November 2025. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability. Growth Opportunities in AI, Multi-Cloud and Sovereign Infrastructure Multi-cloud adoption and sovereign AI initiatives are creating opportunities for hyperscale development, specialized AI-ready facilities and strategic infrastructure partnerships. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services. Thermal management will remain a central investment priority as rack densities increase. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling and hybrid cooling systems are expected to gain adoption across AI and high-performance computing environments. Power availability will also shape future development, encouraging collaboration among hyperscale operators, utilities, renewable energy developers, semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure investors. Global Hyperscale Data Center Market Projected to Reach USD 1.21 Trillion by 2040 as AI Infrastructure Investment Accelerates
The global hyperscale data center market is projected to increase from USD 245.0 billion in 2026 to USD 1.21 trillion by 2040, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 12.1%. Market growth is being driven by artificial intelligence workloads, hyperscale cloud expansion, high-density GPU deployments, data sovereignty requirements and rising demand for energy-efficient digital infrastructure.
Infrastructure priorities are shifting from traditional cloud capacity optimization toward power-intensive AI computing clusters. This transition is increasing demand for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling, high-speed networking, advanced power management and gigawatt-scale data center campuses. Major cloud service providers and infrastructure operators are also integrating renewable energy procurement into development strategies as sustainability regulations and grid constraints influence site selection.
Recent transactions demonstrate the strategic importance of hyperscale infrastructure. Alphabet's acquisition of renewable energy developer Intersect in December 2025 reflected the growing convergence of clean energy and data center development. Industry confidence was further illustrated by the USD 40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers by a consortium comprising BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA and xAI.

Competitive Landscape and Investment Outlook
The hyperscale data center industry is increasingly characterized by vertically integrated cloud and AI infrastructure ecosystems. Leading operators maintain extensive control over computing resources, networking, AI accelerators, software platforms and energy procurement. Competitive differentiation is becoming closely tied to access to power, deployment speed, thermal management, GPU availability and regional cloud coverage.
Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are expected to invest a combined USD 660 billion to USD 690 billion in capital expenditure during 2026. Amazon has projected approximately USD 200 billion in 2026 capital spending, compared with approximately USD 125 billion in the previous year. Microsoft allocated USD 80 billion during 2025 to AI-optimized data centers and Azure infrastructure. Alphabet committed approximately USD 75 billion in 2025 and is expected to raise capital expenditure to between USD 175 billion and USD 185 billion in 2026.
Startup and growth-stage investment is also accelerating. Approximately 70% of data center-focused companies that raised more than USD 500 million completed their latest equity financing rounds during 2024 or 2025. CoreWeave has expanded its AI cloud infrastructure footprint to 32 data center facilities and approximately 250,000 GPUs as of 2025. Vantage Data Centers secured more than USD 2 billion in Series C financing in January 2026 after receiving an additional USD 1.6 billion equity investment in November 2025. Emerald AI is developing intelligent energy management capabilities that coordinate AI workloads with real-time grid availability.
Growth Opportunities in AI, Multi-Cloud and Sovereign Infrastructure
Multi-cloud adoption and sovereign AI initiatives are creating opportunities for hyperscale development, specialized AI-ready facilities and strategic infrastructure partnerships. Enterprises are distributing workloads across multiple platforms to improve resilience, regulatory compliance, performance and risk management. Regional cloud deployments announced or advanced by AWS, Microsoft and Google across Asia-Pacific and Europe during 2025 are expected to support demand for networking equipment, cooling systems, power infrastructure and data center construction services.
Thermal management will remain a central investment priority as rack densities increase. Direct-to-chip liquid cooling, immersion cooling and hybrid cooling systems are expected to gain adoption across AI and high-performance computing environments. Power availability will also shape future development, encouraging collaboration among hyperscale operators, utilities, renewable energy developers, semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure investors.
